newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prompt squeeze bouys naphtha.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Prompt squeeze bouys naphtha.

text.p: Singapore naphtha was steady on Tuesday despite the falls to overnight crude values as regional demand and tight supplies held the market up, traders said.
Traders said overnight August Brent lost 27 cents in London and had regained a mere five cents on Tuesday in London to last trade at $17.87.
The weaker crude was offset by fresh regional demand with buying seen from a Samsung General Chemical, which was heard due to start-up a 40,000 barrel per day naphtha splitter by end July.
Traders said Samsung has recently stepped up its purchases of full-range naphtha, the feedstock for the new plant that will produce paraxylene and benzene.
The new demand aside, traders said firmer prices were also due to the cut in supplies in Indonesia due to the shutdown of a crude unit at the Balikpapan refinery since July 10.
The refinery generally exports three 240,000-barrel cargoes of naphtha a month, traders said.
Indonesian naphtha exports will remain low in August as well as a crude unit at the Cilacap refinery will close from August 13 for about 35 days, traders said.
The tighter regional supplies were also aggravated by the cuts to refining output in Singapore due to poor margins and high stocks of middle distillate.
Currently, about 90,000-bpd of production is lost as a result of these cuts, traders said.
Due to these supply restrictions, traders looking to cover prompt shorts are paying high premiums for the cargoes.
On Monday a Singapore refiner sold a 160,000-barrel early August cargo at $1.00 per barrel above spot Singapore quotes on free-on-board basis, traders said.
The swaps market edged down slightly with August last quoted at $21.25/$21.35 per barrel compared to $21.40/$21.50 on Monday, brokers said.
Gasoline was also steady despite the crude fall with a 95-octane cargo offered at $23.30 per barrel fob Singapore for August 8-12 loading.
